correctness.rationale: Given a new table born when root table occupancy is r, later two-table choices form classical Polya urn (r,1); eventual challenger victory probability h_r=Pr(Beta(1,r)>1/2)=2^-r. Ever strict takeover integrates biased gambler ruin over Beta to g_r=2^-r+r int_0^(1/2) x^r/(1-x)dx, bounded by 2^(1-r). Birth at fixed time j has probability epsilon=1-p and R_(j-1)->j-1 as p->1; two fixed births contribute at most epsilon^2. Need control infinite late-birth union: on no-early-birth history root starts J and couples below by independent Bernoulli J/(2n), giving E 2^-R_n<=2^-J(J/n)^(J/4) and exponential J tail; histories with early births have probability O_J(epsilon) and their conditional late-challenger risk ->0 by finite-state convergence to positive-root-share Polya at p=1. Thus exchanging first-order limit with infinite union is justified. A finite-family squeeze avoids interchanging max over infinitely many tables with n-limit for theta. Summing h_r=1 and sum (g_r-h_r)=1/2 proves slopes. Independent direct series yields g_1=ln2, g_2=0.386294361..., sum g=1.5; not a replacement for late-birth lemma. First-time ties favor root, so strict takeover is correct failure event.

value.rationale: Eventual leadership and eternal leadership are two canonical non-equivalent events in random recursive tree percolation. Their sharp unequal first-order constants quantitatively isolate temporary defeat and recovery, requiring subtle tail control of infinitely many challenger births; this is a motivated probabilistic invariant and not a finite toy calculation.

final_claim: In independent bond-percolation on growing uniform random recursive trees, letting rho(p) denote perpetual root-cluster leadership and theta(p) the n-infinity single-time root leadership limit, the iterated p-up-to-1 slopes are (1-rho)/(1-p)->3/2 and (1-theta)/(1-p)->1; theta-rho=(1-p)/2+o(1-p).
